data.name: Citizen (A1)
data.description: A Citizen is a user of the system who submits reports to be read and responded to by police officers

threats.title: Citizen doesn't own email address
threats.description: The user registers with an email they don't own.
threats.mitigation: - Use email verification code after registration.

threats.title: Bad actor logs in using stolen credentials
threats.description: Bad actor finds a user's email and password (through measures like phishing emails etc) and attempts to use it to log in.
threats.mitigation: - Enforce multi-factor authentication to ensure that stolen credentials can't allow a user to log in with credentials alone.

threats.title: User's session cookie is stolen
threats.description: A bad actor obtains a session cookie belonging to a legitimate authenticated user, allowing them to impersonate a citizen by without knowing their password.
threats.mitigation:
- Short session expiry or cookie-token lifetime
- Session id rotation after privilege changes or re-authentication
- Require re-authentication for sensitive actions
- Use session binding to reject or flag requests where the session is used from a different context

threats.title: Weak Password
threats.description: Passwords can be guessed if they are too weak, or have been reused on another application where a data breach occurred.
threats.mitigation:
- Enforce strong password rules such as 10 characters and at least one of capital letter, number, special character, or pass-phrases
- Limit the number of times a user can attempt to login (so that bad actors have less chances at guessing correctly)

threats.title: Spoofed login session
threats.description: Stolen cookies remain valid indefinitely, letting an attacker impersonate the citizen long after the cookie was stolen
threats.mitigation:
- Have an idle-timeout and absolute-timeout for all session IDs.
- Invalidate a session ID once logout occurs.

threats.title: Non secure session cookie sent back to the Citizen
threats.description: If the response from the login process fails to set the HttpOnly flag on the session cookie, a malicious script running on the front end could read/write to the cookie and allow a Bad Actor to impersonate the citizen.
threats.mitigation: - Use the HttpOnly + Secure flag on cookies to prevent client side javascript code from reading to the cookie. This also prevents writing in most browsers.

threats.title: Account enumeration via error messages
threats.description: The application returns different responses or takes a different amount of time to respond depending on whether an email address is registered, has the wrong password, or hasn't been verified yet. This information can be used to determine which email addresses have accounts on the system.
threats.mitigation:
- Return the same comprehensive error message for all failure cases.
- Add timing delays so that timing differences are not observable.

data.name:
Register 
for MFA (T7)
data.description: This process occurs after email verification and first-time log in (T4)

threats.title: Flooding the process with requests
threats.description: A bad actor could send many requests to the server because it is a process that does not require authentication.
threats.mitigation:
- Rate limiting for requests from the same IP on the reverse proxy.
- Add load balancing to reverse proxy to spread request traffic across servers.

threats.title: Process replaced by scammer
threats.description:
The official registration page has been replaced by another malicious page users are redirected to from scam emails, or text messages, or links posted online.

Specific to Register Process: 
This can mean Bad Actor can get access to the QR code used to enrol in on the authenticator app, allowing them to set the authenticator app up on the user's behalf.
threats.mitigation:
- Buy similar domain names with typos.

Specific to Register MFA process: 
- Bind enrolment to an existing authenticated session.
- Notify the citizen's pre-existing verified channel on any new enrolment, with one-click revoke that collapses the attacker's window even if the QR is captured.

threats.title: Process has been tampered with
threats.description: The process has been altered by an external malicious actor. This can be done by modifying source code and binaries (static tampering), injecting a different process (DLL injection), or memory corruption that can disrupt execution flow (e.g. corrupting heap metadata like function pointers).
threats.mitigation:
- Monitor and keep a record of process ID to identify process restart.
- Add fingerprinting to process, e.g., change time, binary / script hash.
- Monitor process in/out and flag unexpected data patterns, malformed payloads unusual destinations or processes that deviate from usual register behaviour.

threats.title: Process leaks unsafe data via memory
threats.description: Process logs sensitive data, or stores data in unsafe (e.g., shared) memory
threats.mitigation:
- Use type-safe and memory-safe programming language e.g. Java, Rust
- Ensure log entries don't contain sensitive data.
- Monitor process usages and in/out for suspicious activity.

threats.title: Process gets access to restricted resources
threats.description: Process runs at a higher priority level (e.g., permissions, resources), or accesses to assets outside its permission level.
threats.mitigation:
- Apply principle of least privilege for process and used resources.
- Run process on the OS with as few permissions as required, using a dedicated technical account rather than a normal user account with interactive and logon permissions.
- Run in container with dropped capabilities.

threats.title: Injection attack - tampering
threats.description: Malicious data is passed to the process to cause harm to the underlying data, e.g., override data or inject malicious data.
threats.mitigation:
- Decode, normalise, and canonicalise email and password before validation and storage
- Sanitise input for script-like requests, e.g., javascript, SQL, etc.
- Enforce strict Content Security Policy to prevent harmful scripts to be transmitted (e.g., js, py, sh files).
- Add parameterised queries/prepared statements for all DB access.

threats.title: Injection attack - disclosure
threats.description: Malicious data is passed to the process to gain access to or exfiltrate data stored in database.
threats.mitigation:
- Decode, normalise, and canonicalise email and password before validation and storage
- Sanitise input from script-like statements, e.g., javascript, SQL, etc.
- Enforce strict CSP policy to prevent harmful scripts to be transmitted (e.g., js, py, sh files).

threats.title: Expose sensitive data in logs
threats.description: Logs may leak sensitive data such as email, password, IP, and session IDs, when tracing user actions.
threats.mitigation:
- Ensure that all sensitive PII data other than user ID are not logged.
- Conduct regular log audits.

threats.title: MFA enrolment secret exposed via QR code capture
threats.description: The QR code encodes the shared secret used to generate future authentication codes/approvals. If a Bad Actor captures the QR code (e.g. screen-sharing, malware taking a screenshot), they can enrol their own device against the citizen's account.
threats.mitigation:
- Display the QR code only briefly and only after re-authentication.
- Warn the citizen not to share their screen while the QR code is displayed.

data.description: Request for a push notification reaches the operating system of the phone via a TLS connection (D2) that is always open (not modelled here for simplicity). The OS then hands this request to the authenticator app to notify the person

threats.title: Push authentication request tampered with in transit
threats.description: Payload travels over an OS-managed push notification channel between the citizen's device and the push notifications service, rather than a connection the application itself. If  a connection terminates while a payload is sent, and a malicious app or malware on the device can still intercept or spoof the notification.
threats.mitigation:
- Use TLS encrypted channel to protect the payload from tampering in transit. 
- Keep the push notification request minimal so a party with visibility into the decrypted payload cannot meaningfully change what is displayed or trigger unintended actions.
- Have the authenticator app fetch the actual request details (device, location, timestamp) in-app over its own authenticated channel rather than trusting content from the request from the OS.

threats.description: See #56

threats.title: MFA push-notification fatigue
threats.description: A Bad Actor who already has the citizen's password repeatedly triggers login attempts, sending a flood of push approval prompts to the citizen's authenticator app in the hope that the citizen approves one out of confusion, annoyance, or accident, allowing the Bad Actor to be authenticated.
threats.mitigation:
- Require the citizen to enter a number shown on the login screen into the app (number matching) rather than a simple approve/deny tap.
- Rate limit the number of push prompts sent for a single account within a time window.
- Show contextual information in the prompt (approximate location, device, time) to help the citizen recognise unfamiliar requests.
- Temporarily lock the account or require step-up verification after repeated unactioned/denied prompts.

threats.title: Citizen denies approving a fraudulent authentication
threats.description: A citizen who approved a push prompt, intentionally or by mistake, later denies having done so, leaving no way to determine whether the approval was legitimate or the account was compromised.
threats.mitigation:
- Log every push prompt sent and every approval/denial decision, including timestamp, device identifier, and approximate location.
- Notify the citizen via email whenever a new device is approved or an approval occurs from an unfamiliar location.

data.name:
Random
Number
Generator (D8, T7)
data.description: The dependency process that generates randoms to be used for generating session ids, verification code, and seeds.

threats.title: Library replaced with a fake/malicious library
threats.description: Legitimate library replaced with a fake library by an actor, so consuming applications unknowingly pull numbers from an attacker controlled source.
threats.mitigation:
- Code signing - require the library to be crypto-graphically signed by a trusted authority, and verify this signature before load. 
- Add fingerprinting to process, e.g., change time, binary / script hash, and verify at load time or periodically at runtime.
- Use fixed absolute library paths for loading. 
- Use an allow list to declare exactly which library version and path are permitted
- Monitor unexpected restarts or new processes claiming to be the library.

threats.title: Entropy/seed leakage
threats.description: Internal state or seed value of the random number generator is exposed, allowing a bad actor to reconstruct past or predict future random numbers.
threats.mitigation:
- Choose a well audited library (and library version) with no reported vulnerabilities. 
- Monitor the 'health' of the entropy source

threats.title: Generation algorithm makes random number guessable
threats.description: Random number generator uses an algorithm that is not cryptographically secure, meaning even without the internal state being known, a past and future output can be guessed using brute force.
threats.mitigation:
- Prefer libraries that use algorithms specified in NIST SP 800-90A/B/C or equivalent, which have been formally analyzed for prediction resistance.
- Ensure that library uses an algorithm such that compromise of current state does not allow reconstruction of past outputs or prediction of future outputs.

threats.title: Process has been tampered with
threats.description: See #24

threats.title: Injection attack - tampering
threats.description: See #26
threats.mitigation: - Choose a well audited library (and library version) with no reported vulnerabilities.

threats.title: Push Notification Service replaced with malicious service
threats.description: A Bad Actor stands up a malicious endpoint that mimics the Push Notification Service, causing the Login process to send authentication push requests to an attacker-controlled service instead of the legitimate one.
threats.mitigation:
- Use mutually authenticated TLS between the Login process and the Push Notification Service.
- Pin or verify the provider's certificate/public key.
- Use signed API credentials issued by the provider and rotate them regularly.

threats.title: Authentication metadata disclosed to third-party provider
threats.description: Push notifications are typically relayed through a third-party provider (e.g. Apple APNs, Google FCM) outside the application's direct control. This can expose login context such as device token, approximate location, or timing of sign-in attempts to that third party.
threats.mitigation:
- Keep the notification payload minimal
- Review the data-handling agreement/terms of the push provider.

threats.title: Push Notification Service unavailable or flooded
threats.description: A Bad Actor floods the Push Notification Service with requests, or the third-party provider experiences an outage, preventing authentication prompts from being delivered and locking citizens out of login.
threats.mitigation:
- Rate limit push requests per account and per source IP.
- Monitor provider status and delivery success rate, and alert on anomalies.
- Choose a trusted push notification service.

data.name: Device Data Store (T8)
data.description: Stores information about the devices that use the application, such as device_id, associated user_id, device_token for push notification, date enrolled etc.

threats.title: Exfiltrate data
threats.description: An unregistered or unprivileged process or user tries to get access to the datastore.
threats.mitigation:
- Use strong credentials for database access stored in secured password vaults.
- Credentials are passed at runtime from environment variables for most DB owners / users with least privilege principle.
- Disable default DB user.
- Separate between read and read/write permissions.
- Monitor for unusual activity, e.g., bulk data accessed, unusual number of simultaneous requests or connections.

NOTE: Copied straight from example

threats.title: DB is accessed and tampered with
threats.description: A bad actor or process tamper the datastore directly.
threats.mitigation:
- Allow full access to datastore to only a restricted set of personnel.
- Store strong credentials in password vaults.
- Monitor for and log all direct command line accesses to the datastore.
- Keep regular backups in a separate location.

threats.title: DB is unreachable
threats.description: A bad actor floods the datastore with requests and overloads the database connection pool, preventing access to the database.
threats.mitigation:
- Monitor suspicious requests and disallow requests from abusing local IPs or ban abusing user.
- Allow for replication and deployment with limited downtime when the load increases slightly.
- Use a pool of connection with query timeouts to release resources fast even for unsuccessful queries.
- Set a maximum number of connections allowed, with a queue.
- Set a limit to the memory used by each query.
- Monitor disk and CPU usage.

threats.title: Citizen PII stored unencrypted
threats.description: If the database disk is unencrypted and obtained by a Bad Actor, the data can be read directly.
threats.mitigation:
- Encrypt the database at rest.
- Keep the database isolated to the app host - don't serve access to the database over the network

threats.title: No audit trail of account data changes
threats.description: Without an audit log, a citizen could deny changes they have made to their account credentials. There is also no way of tracking when and whether a Bad Actor has submitted changes to a citizens account.
threats.mitigation:
- Maintain an audit log of account change events such as registration and verification.
- Include timestamps in logs
- Monitor logs for abnormalities

diagrams.title: Request More Info via Stored Report Message

data.name:
Police Officer
(A3, T6)
data.description: A3 Police officer. T6 logged-in police officer: searches and views all reports, emails owners requesting more information and closes reports. Assumed unable to create or edit reports.

threats.title: Officer account compromised
threats.description: An attacker holding officer credentials, or an intercepted officer session, reads every report in the system and can close any of them.
threats.mitigation: Serve officer routes over HTTPS with HSTS, apply a short idle timeout and alert on unusual sign in locations.

threats.title: Privileged officer action not recorded
threats.description: There is no record of which officer performed a privileged action like closures or requesting further information
threats.mitigation: Write an audit record of officer ID, action, related text, timestamp, and protect the logs (X9) from the T6 role.

data.name:
Citizen / Report Owner
(A1, T4/T5)
data.description: A1 Citizen. T4 logged in citizen, T5 owner of the reports they created. Registers, submits reports with images, views and edits their own open reports and generates share links.

threats.title: Report owner's mailbox controlled by an attacker
threats.description: An attacker who controls the report owner's mailbox receives the information request (X6) and the closure notification (X7)
threats.mitigation: Re-verify the address whenever it is changed, and keep incident detail out of  email by linking back to the authenticated page.

data.name:
Request More Info
(E13)
data.description: CHANGED. E13 Request more info. The officer writes the information request in the application and it is written to the Report Message Store as a ReportMessage (report, officer, body, created_at) rather than being sent. The outbound email is reduced to a fixed template containing no officer supplied content.

threats.title: Email header injection
threats.description: Injecting extra headers, letting the message be redirected or additional recipients added.
threats.mitigation: Include input validataion and construct headers through the mail library rather than by string building.

threats.title: Information request sent to the wrong owner
threats.description: The recipient address is taken from the request instead of the stored report, so report detail reaches an attacker chosen mailbox.
threats.mitigation: Resolve the recipient from the report's stored owner in D6, never from client supplied input.

threats.title: Report content disclosed in cleartext email
threats.description: Mail delivery to the citizen's external provider is outside the system's control so any incident detail ends up in an external mailbox in cleartext.
threats.mitigation: Keep incident detail out of the message body, send a short notice identifying the report by reference with a link back to the authenticated page

threats.title: NEW - Officer supplied body stored without sanitisation
threats.description: The body is free text written by an officer and is later rendered on the report page. Script in the body would run in the report owner's browser.
threats.mitigation:
- Escape the message body on output
- Validate the body before presenting to user

threats.title: NEW - Message written without recording the officer
threats.description: If the officer field is not set from the authenticated session, then the police officer who wrote the message can not be identified
threats.mitigation: - Set officer and created_at server side from the session, never from the request.

data.name:
Email Dispatcher
(D10)
data.description: CHANGED. D10 Email dispatcher. For information requests it now sends only a fixed template stating that there is an update on one of the citizen's reports and that the citizen should log in to view it. No officer supplied content and no links are included.

threats.title: Mail credentials disclosed
threats.description: Mail service credentials stored in the application configuration are read by an attacker, who can then send mail as the service.
threats.mitigation:
- Keep configuration outside the web root, readable only by the T7 account, and rotate credentials.
- Use secure secrets vault and apply the principle of least privilege.

threats.title: Dispatcher abused to send arbitrary mail
threats.description: An attacker who can reach the dispatcher sends convincing mail that appears to come from the service, enabling phishing against citizens.
threats.mitigation: - Authenticate which accounts have access to the mail service,

threats.title: Email queue flooded
threats.description: Repeated information requests or closures generate enough mail to exhaust the sending quota, delaying verification email (X5) and blocking registration.
threats.mitigation:
- Rate limit outbound mail per officer and per report.
- Monitor queue size for abnormalities

threats.title: NEW - Notification confirms an address belongs to a report owner
threats.description: The notification tells anyone reading the mailbox that this address has an open report with the police.
threats.mitigation: - Do not name the report, the incident or the officer in the template.

data.name:
View / Edit Report
(E7)
data.description: CHANGED. E7 View and edit report page. The report owner (T5) now also reads officer messages here and responds by editing the report as they do currently. Sets read_at on a message when it is displayed.

threats.title: Insecure direct object reference
threats.description: A user could change the report ID to access or edit another citizen's report if the system does not check who owns it.
threats.mitigation: - Derive the owner from the authenticated session and perform a server-side ownership check on the identifier for every report request.

threats.title: Editing closed reports
threats.description: A crafted request could bypass a hidden edit button if the server does not enforce report state, so a closed report can still be modified.
threats.mitigation: - Always read the closed status with the record and reject updates server-side when the report is closed.

threats.title: Mass assignment of closed status
threats.description: A citizen may attempt to manipulate protected fields such as closed status.
threats.mitigation: - Allow-list editable fields and never accept closed status from the citizen.

threats.title: Stored cross-site scripting in report description - Tampering
threats.description: A user could enter malicious script in a report description that runs when the report is viewed, and tampers with page content and behaviour.
threats.mitigation:
- Safely encode the report description when displaying it so it is treated as text rather than code.
- Use a strict CSP to prevent interaction with other domains
- Use HttpOnly cookies so that a XSS attack cannot tamper with session ids and other important data.

threats.title: Stored cross-site scripting in report description - Information Disclosure
threats.description: A user could enter malicious script in a report description that runs when the report is viewed, and tampers with page content and behaviour.
threats.mitigation:
- Safely encode the report description when displaying it so it is treated as text rather than code.
- Use a strict CSP to prevent interaction with other domains
- Use HttpOnly cookies so that a XSS attack cannot tamper with session ids and other important data.

threats.title: NEW - Messages shown to a citizen who does not own the report
threats.description: If the message can be found by report ID alone, any logged-in citizen (T4) who guesses a report ID reads the officer messages for it.
threats.mitigation: - Ensure the report and the report messages are only available to authenticated owner.

data.name:
Report Store
(D6)
data.description: D6 Database. Asset: report content - date, time, location, description, created time, closed status and owner / created_by. Reachable only from the application (T7 -> T8). In this proposal it is also the source of the owner address used for the notification, so the address is never taken from the officer's request.

threats.title: Unauthorised report disclosure
threats.description: Direct database access could expose sensitive report information.
threats.mitigation: Restrict database access, use least privilege and protect data at rest.

threats.title: Direct report tampering
threats.description: Database access could bypass application authorisation and modify reports.
threats.mitigation: Restrict direct database access and audit administrative changes.

data.name:
Report Message
Store
data.description: NEW. Append only store holding ReportMessage records: report, officer, body, created_at and read_at. Because the message must be stored for the citizen to read it in the application, a record of which officer wrote what, and when, exists as a consequence of the change rather than as a separate mechanism alongside it.

threats.title: NEW - Officers delete report messages
threats.description: An officer removes the record of an information request they sent, so there is no longer any evidence.
threats.mitigation:
- Make the store append only
- Do not grant officer roles delete permission on the message table

threats.title: NEW - Bulk harvesting of police messages
threats.description: An unprivileged process or user reads the message store directly and obtains the body of every information request sent about every report
threats.mitigation:
- Least privilege database credentials held only by the application
- Monitor for bulk reads of the message table

threats.title: NEW - Message store tampered with directly
threats.description: Direct database access is used to alter or insert a message, bypassing every application check on who may write one
threats.mitigation:
- Restrict write access to the application identity (T7) only.
- Keep the store append only so edits are not possible.

threats.title: NEW - Message store unreachable
threats.description: If the store is unavailable the officer cannot record a request and the citizen cannot read one, so the information request feature stops working entirely.
threats.mitigation:
- Monitor availability and alert on failure.
- Do not send a notification email if the message was not stored.

data.name: officer session + report ID + information request text
data.description: The officer's session, the report ID and the free text body of the information request. Unchanged by this proposal: the officer still writes the text, it is simply stored instead of emailed.

threats.title: Information request text observed in transit
threats.description: The text may quote incident detail from the report.
threats.mitigation: Use HTTPS protocol only with HSTS .

labels: officer session + report ID + information request text

data.name: notification trigger + owner address
data.description: CHANGED. Only the recipient address and a template identifier are handed to the dispatcher. No officer supplied content crosses this flow any more.

threats.title: NEW - Officer content reaches the dispatcher
threats.description: If any officer supplied field is still passed through to the dispatcher, phishing can still occur.
threats.mitigation:
- Pass only the address and a fixed template ID.
- Reject any free text on the dispatch path.

data.name: fixed-template notification email (X6)
data.description: CHANGED. X6. A fixed template saying only that there is an update on one of the citizen's reports and that they should log in to view it. Carries no officer supplied content and no links.

threats.title: Report content disclosed in cleartext email
threats.description: The information request email leaves the system on this flow. See the identically titled threat on Request More Info (E13).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Request More Info (E13).

threats.title: NEW - Fixed template cloned by an attacker
threats.description: Because the notification is identical every time, an attacker can clone it and add a malicious link, and the citizen has no way to tell the copy from the real one.
threats.mitigation: - Include no links in the template at all, so that any mail containing a link is visibly not from SecureReports.

threats.title: Insecure direct object reference
threats.description: This flow carries the client-supplied report ID that can be altered. See the identically titled threat on View / Edit Report (E7) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on View / Edit Report (E7).

threats.title: Edited report content observed in transit
threats.description: Both the retrieved report and the edited version cross the internet boundary in this exchange.
threats.mitigation: HTTPS only with HSTS (see model assumptions).

data.name: report details + officer messages (X1)
data.description: CHANGED. X1. The report page returned to the owner, now also carrying the officer messages held for that report.

threats.title: NEW - Message body rendered without escaping
threats.description: The officer written body is rendered in the owner's browser. Unescaped output would run as script in the owner's session.
threats.mitigation: - Escape the body on output.

data.name: message lookup
data.description: NEW. Reads the messages held for the report the owner is viewing.

threats.title: NEW - Data or query altered in transit
threats.description: The message lookup is altered between the application and the database.
threats.mitigation:
- Encrypted database connection.
- Database reachable only from the application host.

threats.title: NEW - Data is read in transit
threats.description: The message lookup is read on the internal network.
threats.mitigation: - Encrypted database connection.

data.name: store report message (report, officer, body, created_at)
data.description: NEW. The ReportMessage record written to the append only message store. This write, not a separate audit mechanism, is what creates the record of who asked for what.

threats.title: NEW - Data or query altered in transit
threats.description: See #318
threats.mitigation: See #318

threats.title: NEW - Data is read in transit
threats.description: See #319
threats.mitigation: See #319

threats.title: Editing closed reports
threats.description: This flow is where the closed status must be carried into the edit decision. See the identically titled threat on View / Edit Report (E7) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on View / Edit Report (E7).

data.name: stored messages (officer, body, created_at)
data.description: NEW. The stored messages returned for display on the report page.

threats.title: NEW - Data or query altered in transit
threats.description: See #318
threats.mitigation: See #318

threats.title: NEW - Data is read in transit
threats.description: See #319
threats.mitigation: See #319

diagrams.title: Reports Sharing Expiry and Revocation
diagrams.placeholder: Updated E8-E9 report-sharing model. Share links now have a server-enforced expiration time and can be revoked by the report owner. E9 checks token validity, expiration and revocation before returning the report.

data.name: Citizen / Report Owner (T5)
data.description: Authenticated report owner who can create and revoke share links for their own reports.

data.name: Share Link Recipient (T3)
data.description: Unauthenticated user who possesses a valid share token and is permitted to view the associated report.

data.name: Create / Manage Share Link (E8)
data.description: E8 Share link creation and revocation. Creates a cryptographically random token for a report owned by the citizen, assigns an expiry time, stores the token association and allows the owner to revoke the token.

threats.title: Unauthorised revocation of another user's share link
threats.description: A citizen could attempt to revoke a share token belonging to a report they do not own by manipulating the token or report identifier in the revocation request.
threats.mitigation: Require authentication and perform a server-side ownership check before changing the revocation state of a share token. The authenticated user must own the associated report.

threats.title: Creating a link for someone else's report
threats.description: A citizen submits another citizen's report ID to E8 and obtains a working share link for a report they do not own.
threats.mitigation: Server side ownership check before creating the token.

data.name: Share Token Store (D6)
data.description: Stores hashed share tokens, associated report IDs, creation time, expiry time and revocation state. Plaintext token is returned only when the link is created and is not stored in usable form.

threats.title: Share tokens stored in usable form
threats.description: If plaintext share tokens are stored, anyone obtaining read access to the token store obtains working share links.
threats.mitigation: Store only a cryptographic hash of each share token. The plaintext token should only be returned to the report owner when the link is created.

data.name: Validate Token and Show Report (E9)
data.description: E9 Share link page. Receives a secret token and checks that it exists, has not expired and has not been revoked before retrieving and displaying the associated report.

threats.title: Expired or revoked token accepted
threats.description: If E9 does not correctly enforce expiration and revocation server-side, a leaked token could continue providing access after the owner intended the link to stop working.
threats.mitigation: On every request, validate token existence, compare the current time with expires_at, and reject tokens with a non-null revoked_at value before retrieving the report.

threats.title: Token enumeration
threats.description: An attacker could repeatedly submit candidate tokens and use different responses to determine which tokens are valid.
threats.mitigation: Use high-entropy cryptographically random tokens, rate-limit token validation attempts and return generic responses for invalid, expired and revoked tokens.

threats.title: Closed report remains accessible
threats.description: A share link created while the report was open keeps returning content after closure if report state is not re-checked during share-link authorisation.
threats.mitigation: Re-check the report state at read time and refuse the share view for closed reports.

data.name: Report Database (D6)
data.description: Stores report information associated with the validated share token.

data.name: revoke share link request
data.description: Authenticated report owner requests that an existing share token be revoked.

threats.title: Revocation request targets another report
threats.description: The client could modify the token or report identifier in the request to attempt to revoke a share link belonging to another citizen.
threats.mitigation: Use the authenticated session to identify the requester and verify ownership of the report associated with the token before revocation.

data.name: revoked_at update
data.description: E8 records the revocation time for the selected share token.

threats.title: Unauthorised revocation state change
threats.description: A token could be incorrectly marked revoked or unrevoked by an unauthorised request.
threats.mitigation: Allow only authenticated owners to initiate revocation and do not expose direct client control over the revoked_at value.

data.name: token hash + expiry + revocation state
data.description: E9 retrieves the token record to determine whether the token exists, has expired or has been revoked.

threats.title: Incomplete validity check
threats.description: If E9 checks the token but fails to check expiry or revocation state, a leaked token can continue to access the report after the owner intended access to end.
threats.mitigation: Require all three conditions before access: token exists, current time is before expires_at, and revoked_at is null.

data.name: create share link request
data.description: Authenticated report owner requests creation of a share link for their report.

data.name: share URL
data.description: The newly generated share URL returned to the report owner.

threats.title: Leaked or forwarded share token
threats.description: A recipient can forward or disclose the share token, allowing anyone who obtains it to access the report while the token remains valid.
threats.mitigation: Use high-entropy tokens, enforce expiration, and allow the report owner to revoke the token.

data.name: token hash + report ID + expiry
data.description: E8 stores the hashed token together with its associated report and server-generated expiry time.

threats.title: Token metadata manipulated
threats.description: Expiry or report association could be modified if the application or database permissions allow unauthorised writes.
threats.mitigation: Use least-privilege database permissions and perform all token metadata changes through authorised server-side operations.

data.name: validated report lookup
data.description: E9 retrieves only the report associated with a successfully validated share token.

threats.title: Token-to-report association bypass
threats.description: A flaw could allow the requester to manipulate a report identifier and use a valid token to retrieve a different report.
threats.mitigation: Retrieve the report ID only from the validated token record and never accept a separate client-supplied report ID for the shared-report lookup.

data.name: share token
data.description: The secret token supplied by an unauthenticated recipient to access the shared report.

threats.title: Token guessing or brute force
threats.description: An attacker could submit guessed tokens in an attempt to obtain unauthorised access to reports.
threats.mitigation: Generate tokens using a cryptographically secure random number generator with sufficient entropy and rate-limit validation attempts.

data.name: shared report X2
data.description: Report content returned to the share-link recipient only after token validation, expiry check and revocation check.

threats.title: Report disclosed after token should be invalid
threats.description: The shared report could be returned even after the token has expired or been revoked if E9 performs validation incorrectly or uses stale token state.
threats.mitigation: Perform validation immediately before retrieving and returning the report. Do not cache authorised report responses beyond the token validity period.

diagrams.title: Verification Code Expiry and Request New Link

data.name: Citizen
data.description: A citizen who has registered an account and must verify their email address before they can log in. In this proposal the citizen may also request a replacement verification link once the original has expired.

threats.title: Weak password
threats.description: Passwords can be guessed if they are too weak, or have been reused on another application where a data breach occurred.
threats.mitigation:
- Enforce strong password rules such as 10 characters and at least one of capital letter, number, special character, or pass-phrases
- Limit the number of times a user can attempt to login (so that bad actors have less chances at guessing correctly)

threats.title: Citizen doesn't own email address
threats.description: The user registers with an email they don't own.
threats.mitigation:
- Use email verification code after registration.
- (PROPOSED CHANGE) verification_code_expiry bounds the window in which a verification link for an address the registrant does not own remains usable to 10 minutes, so a mailbox compromised after that window no longer activates the account.

threats.title: Bad actor logs in using stolen credentials
threats.description: Bad actors finds a user's email and password (through measures like phishing emails etc) and attempts to use it to log in.

threats.title: User's session cookie is stolen
threats.description: A bad actor obtains a session cookie belonging to a legitimate authenticated user, allowing them to impersonate a citizen by without knowing their password.
threats.mitigation:
- Short session expiry or cookie-token lifetime
- Session id rotation after privilege changes or re-authentication
- Require re-authentication for sensitive actions
- Use session binding to reject or flag requests where the session is used from a different context

data.name:
Email
Service
Provider
data.description: Third-party email service that delivers the verification link to the citizen's mailbox. Outside the SecureReports trust boundary. The mail transport chain (MTA, mailbox) is collapsed into this element as it is unchanged by this proposal.

threats.title: Verification email spoofed as coming from SecureReports
threats.description: The absence of SPF/DKIM/DMARC configuration allows Bad Actors to forge a verification email as coming from SecureReports.
threats.mitigation:
- Configure SPF, DKIM, DMARC on the domain used to send verification emails
- Monitor DMARC reports for unauthorised sending attempts

threats.title: Email vendor becomes comprimised through tampering
threats.description: The email service and is assumed third-party infrastructure. If the vendor is compromised (e.g. its API keys are stolen), an attacker can send mail as SecureReports, or read mail in transit.
threats.mitigation:
- Apply the principle of least privilege when storing API keys
- Rotate keys regularly
- Audit the third-party software's security
- Store keys in a secret vault

threats.title: Phishing SecureReports verify email clone
threats.description: A Bad Actor impersonates the legitimate SecureReports verification email with a link that directs citizens to a illegitimate site that harvests their email, password, and/or other personal data.
threats.mitigation: - Purchase all look-alike domains.

threats.title: Verification token is retained in provider logs
threats.description: If the email provider logs message content/metadata, it can become exposed later if the email provider is compromised.
threats.mitigation:
- Configure the provider's log retention period to a minimum
- Conduct regular security audits of the third-party email provider
- Invalidate the link once used by the citizen
- (PROPOSED CHANGE) A token retained in provider logs is only usable for 10 minutes after issue, so the value of a later log compromise is bounded.

threats.title: MTA becomes comprimised
threats.description: The MTA is assumed third-party infrastructure. If the vendor is compromised (e.g. its API keys are stolen), an attacker can send mail as SecureReports.
threats.mitigation:
- Apply the principle of least privilege when storing API keys
- Rotate keys regularly
- Audit the third-party software's security

threats.title: Verification link read from a shared mailbox
threats.description: The verification email may be read by anyone with access to the citizen's mailbox. A Bad Actor may click on the link to also verify the citizen's account and gain information though the verification flow.
threats.mitigation:
- Invalidate verification links once used by the citizen
- (PROPOSED CHANGE) A link read from a shared mailbox is only usable within the 10 minute expiry window; after that the reader is refused and must request a new link, which is delivered to the same mailbox rather than to them.

data.name:
Request New
Verification Link
data.description: NEW. Reached from the 'Didn't get your verification code?' button shown unconditionally on the login page. Takes an email address, invalidates any verification code already held for that account, stores a new code with verification_code_expiry set to 10 minutes from now, and sends a new verification link. The response is identical whether or not an account exists.

threats.title: NEW - Resend endpoint abused to exhaust email quota
threats.description: An attacker may repeatedly request new verification codes, exhausting the email sending quota and delaying delivery of verification emails for other users. Because the request form is unauthenticated and visible on the login page, no account is needed to reach it.
threats.mitigation:
- Rate limit the number of new verification codes that may be requested per email address, and per source IP address
- Cap the total number of verification emails sent to a single address per timeframe

threats.title: NEW - Previously issued verification codes remain valid after reissue
threats.description: If issuing a new verification code does not invalidate the codes already issued for that account, every code ever sent stays usable.
threats.mitigation:
- Delete all previously issued verification codes for the account whenever a new code is issued.
- Enforce at the data layer that each account holds at most one valid verification code at a time.

threats.title: NEW - Resend endpoint used to enumerate registered email addresses
threats.description: An attacker could submit candidate email addresses to the request-new-link endpoint and use differences in the response to learn which addresses already have an account.
threats.mitigation: - Return an identical response body and status code whether or not an account exists for the submitted address

threats.title: NEW - Process replaced by scammer
threats.description: See #178 (same threat on a different element in this diagram).
threats.mitigation: - As for #178.

threats.title: NEW - Process has been tampered with
threats.description: See #164 (same threat on a different element in this diagram).
threats.mitigation: - As for #164.

threats.title: NEW - Injection attack - tampering
threats.description: See #166 (same threat on a different element in this diagram).
threats.mitigation: - As for #166.

threats.title: NEW - Process leaks data via unsafe memory
threats.description: See #181 (same threat on a different element in this diagram).
threats.mitigation: - As for #181.

threats.title: NEW - Injection attack - disclosure
threats.description: See #182 (same threat on a different element in this diagram).
threats.mitigation: - As for #182.

threats.title: NEW - Expose sensitive data in logs
threats.description: See #183 (same threat on a different element in this diagram).
threats.mitigation: - As for #183.

threats.title: NEW - Process gets access to restricted resources
threats.description: See #184 (same threat on a different element in this diagram).
threats.mitigation: - As for #184.

data.name: Verify Email
data.description: CHANGED. Redeems the verification code from the link. In this proposal it must check verification_code_expiry as well as the code itself: if the current server time is past the expiry, verification is refused and the citizen is shown a message telling them to request a new link.

threats.title: Flooding the verify email process with requests
threats.description: A bad actor could send many requests to the server because it is a process that does not require authentication.
threats.mitigation:
- Rate limiting for requests from the same IP on the reverse proxy.
- Add load balancing to reverse proxy to spread request traffic across servers.

threats.title: Verification process replaced by scammer
threats.description: The official registration page has been replaced by another malicious page users are redirected to from scam emails, or text messages, or links posted online.
threats.mitigation: - Buy similar domain names with typos.

threats.title: Process has been tampered with
threats.description: See #164 (same threat on a different element in this diagram).
threats.mitigation: - As for #164.

threats.title: Injection attack - tampering
threats.description: See #166 (same threat on a different element in this diagram).
threats.mitigation: - As for #166.

threats.title: Process leaks data via unsafe memory
threats.description: Process logs sensitive data, or stores data in unsafe (e.g., shared) memory
threats.mitigation:
- Use type-safe and memory-safe programming language e.g. Java, Rust
- Ensure log entries don't contain sensitive data.
- Monitor process usages and in/out for suspicious activity.

threats.title: Injection attack - disclosure
threats.description: Malicious data is passed to the process to gain access to or exfiltrate data stored in database.
threats.mitigation:
- Decode, normalise, and canonicalise email and password before validation and storage
- Sanitise input from script-like statements, e.g., javascript, SQL, etc.
- Enforce strict CSP policy to prevent harmful scripts to be transmitted (e.g., js, py, sh files).

threats.title: Expose sensitive data in logs
threats.description: Logs may leak sensitive data such as email, password, IP, and session IDs, when tracing user actions.
threats.mitigation:
- Ensure that all sensitive PII data other than user ID are not logged.
- Conduct regular log audits.

threats.title: Process gets access to restricted resources
threats.description: Process runs at a higher priority level (e.g., permissions, resources), or accesses to assets outside its permission level.
threats.mitigation:
- Apply principle of least privilege for process and used resources.
- Run process on the OS with as few permissions as required, using a dedicated technical account rather than a normal user account with interactive and logon permissions.
- Run in container with dropped capabilities.

threats.title: NEW - Expiry field is stored but never evaluated at redemption
threats.description: The verification_code_expiry field exists on the citizen record but the verification process does not evaluate it when the code is redeemed.
threats.mitigation: - Evaluate verification_code_expiry in the same server-side check as the verification code, and reject the request if the code has expired.

data.name:
Random
Number
Generator
data.description: Generates the verification code. Unchanged by this proposal, but included because the request-new-link flow needs a fresh code from it. Code entropy remains a primary defence against guessing; expiry only bounds the guessing window.

threats.title: Library replaced with a fake/malicious library
threats.description: Legitimate library replaced with a fake library by an actor, so consuming applications unknowingly pull numbers from an attacker controlled source.
threats.mitigation:
- Code signing - require the library to be crypto-graphically signed by a trusted authority, and verify this signature before load. 
- Add fingerprinting to process, e.g., change time, binary / script hash, and verify at load time or periodically at runtime.
- Use fixed absolute library paths for loading. 
- Use an allow list to declare exactly which library version and path are permitted
- Monitor unexpected restarts or new processes claiming to be the library.

threats.title: Entropy/seed leakage
threats.description: Internal state or seed value of the random number generator is exposed, allowing a bad actor to reconstruct past or predict future random numbers.
threats.mitigation:
- Choose a well audited library (and library version) with no reported vulnerabilities. 
- Monitor the 'health' of the entropy source

threats.title: Generation algorithm makes random number guessable
threats.description: Random number generator uses an algorithm that is not cryptographically secure, meaning even without the internal state being known, a past and future output can be guessed using brute force.
threats.mitigation:
- Prefer libraries that use algorithms specified in NIST SP 800-90A/B/C or equivalent, which have been formally analyzed for prediction resistance.
- Ensure that library uses an algorithm such that compromise of current state does not allow reconstruction of past outputs or prediction of future outputs.
- (PROPOSED CHANGE) Expiry bounds the time available to brute force a guessable code to 10 minutes. It complements, and does not replace, code entropy and rate limiting, which remain the primary defences against guessing.

threats.title: Process has been tampered with
threats.description: The process has been altered by an external malicious actor. This can be done by modifying source code and binaries (static tampering), injecting a different process (DLL injection), or memory corruption that can disrupt execution flow (e.g. corrupting heap metadata like function pointers).
threats.mitigation:
- Monitor and keep a record of process ID to identify process restart.
- Add fingerprinting to process, e.g., change time, binary / script hash.
- Monitor process in/out and flag unexpected data patterns, malformed payloads unusual destinations or processes that deviate from usual register behaviour.

threats.title: Injection attack - tampering
threats.description: Malicious data is passed to the process to cause harm to the underlying data, e.g., override data or inject malicious data.
threats.mitigation: - Choose a well audited library (and library version) with no reported vulnerabilities.

data.name:
Citizen Information
Data Store
data.description: CHANGED. Holds the citizen record. Gains a verification_code_expiry field (a time, set to 10 minutes after the verification code is issued) alongside the existing email address, hashed password, verification code and is_verified status.

threats.title: Exfiltrate data
threats.description: An unregistered or unprivileged process or user tries to get access to the datastore.
threats.mitigation:
- Use strong credentials for database access stored in secured password vaults.
- Credentials are passed at runtime from environment variables for most DB owners / users with least privilege principle.
- Disable default DB user.
- Separate between read and read/write permissions.
- Monitor for unusual activity, e.g., bulk data accessed, unusual number of simultaneous requests or connections.

NOTE: Copied straight from example

threats.title: DB is accessed and tampered with
threats.description: A bad actor or process tamper the datastore directly.
threats.mitigation:
- Allow full access to datastore to only a restricted set of personnel.
- Store strong credentials in password vaults.
- Monitor for and log all direct command line accesses to the datastore.
- Keep regular backups in a separate location.

threats.title: DB is unreachable
threats.description: A bad actor floods the datastore with requests and overloads the database connection pool, preventing access to the database.
threats.mitigation:
- Monitor suspicious requests and disallow requests from abusing local IPs or ban abusing user.
- Allow for replication and deployment with limited downtime when the load increases slightly.
- Use a pool of connection with query timeouts to release resources fast even for unsuccessful queries.
- Set a maximum number of connections allowed, with a queue.
- Set a limit to the memory used by each query.
- Monitor disk and CPU usage.

threats.title: Citizen PII stored unencrypted
threats.description: If the database disk is unencrypted and obtained by a Bad Actor, the data can be read directly.
threats.mitigation:
- Encrypt the database at rest.
- Keep the database isolated to the app host - don't serve access to the database over the network

threats.title: No audit trail of account data changes
threats.description: Without an audit log, a citizen could deny changes they have made to their account credentials. There is also no way of tracking when and whether a Bad Actor has submitted changes to a citizens account.
threats.mitigation:
- Maintain an audit log of account change events such as registration and verification.
- Include timestamps in logs
- Monitor logs for abnormalities
- (PROPOSED CHANGE) Issue, reissue and expiry of verification codes are new events that must appear in the same audit log.

data.name: SecureReports application trust boundary
data.description: Separates the SecureReports application processes and database from the citizen's browser and the third-party email provider.

data.name: request_new_link_request
data.description: Email address submitted from the 'Didn't get your verification code?' form. Unauthenticated.

threats.title: NEW - Flooding the network with traffic
threats.description: See #224 (same threat on a different element in this diagram).
threats.mitigation: - As for #224.

threats.title: NEW - Request new link request is changed in transit
threats.description: Request URL query parameters or body is tampered with by a bad actor.
threats.mitigation: - Use HTTPS so data is encrypted in transit

threats.title: NEW - Submitted email address exposed to a bad actor
threats.description: Email address and password is accessed by a bad actor on the network, allowing them to steal the user's credentials.
threats.mitigation:
- Use HTTPS to send data over the network
- Use verification code to ensure stolen credentials cannot be used to log in.

data.name: new_verification_code
data.description: Freshly generated verification code for the replacement link.

data.name: invalidate_old_code_+_store_new_code_and_expiry
data.description: Deletes any verification code already held for the account and writes the new code together with verification_code_expiry set to 10 minutes from now.

threats.title: Data or query altered in transit
threats.description: Bad actor alters query in transit (e.g. adding DROP tables to the query) or alters the data in the query to be incorrect (e.g. updating the query to set is_verified = true)
threats.mitigation:
- Use local private network.
- Use certificates to authenticate originating machine.
-  Use prepared statements on the caller side to minimise chances of effects of tampered data.
- Use TLS/SSL encryption for all database connections.

threats.title: Data is read in transit
threats.description: A bad actor captures the data in transit
threats.mitigation:
- Use a secure private network
- Use TLS/SSL encryption for all database connections.

threats.title: Wire is overloaded by request
threats.description: The wire is overloaded by requests in the private network.
threats.mitigation:
- Monitor network activity for suspicious patterns, e.g., corrupted processes
- Drop suspicious packets and ban originating IPs (local firewalling)

data.name: new_verification_link
data.description: Replacement verification link handed to the email provider for delivery. Leaves the SecureReports trust boundary.

threats.title: Verification link altered in transit
threats.description: A Bad Actor may observe and modify the verification link in transit, swapping the token to prevent a user from verifying their account, or altering the url so the citizen will be brought to a phishing page.
threats.mitigation: - Use HTTPS (or another encrypted protocol) so data is encrypted in transit

threats.title: Request-new-link flood exhausts the email API
threats.description: Mass automated registrations can cause the Server's API limit to be reached or overload the email service provider
threats.mitigation:
- Rate limit the registration request before the call to the ESP is performed.
- Monitor API usage limits
- Log traffic and audit logs regularly to detect anomalies.
- (PROPOSED CHANGE) The request-new-link form is a second, unauthenticated path to the email API and must be rate limited in the same way as registration.

data.name: uniform_resend_response
data.description: Response shown to the submitter. Identical whether or not an account exists for the submitted address, so the form does not reveal which addresses are registered.

threats.title: Error messages reveal information about system state
threats.description:
An error message could contain information such as 
- server software & version
- file system paths
- stack traces
- sensitive information such as email and password
threats.mitigation:
- Don't have revealing error messages
- Use HTTPS (or another encrypted protocol) to send data over the network.

threats.title: Verification link intercepted in transit via SMTP

- Invalidate the link once used by the citizen
- (PROPOSED CHANGE) An intercepted link is only usable within the 10 minute expiry window.

threats.mitigation: - Obscure the verification link in the email as a hyperlinked button or styled link text rather than displaying the raw URL.
